headline: [ACTION NEEDED] Claude Mythos autonomously finds thousands of zero-days across every major OS and browser; Gemma 4 open + on-device (256K ctx, Apache 2.0)

developments.title: Claude Mythos Preview: autonomous zero-day discovery at scale — 72.4% exploit conversion rate
developments.source: anthropic.com/glasswing (primary); red.anthropic.com/2026/mythos-preview (system card); red.anthropic.com/2026/exploit (CVE-2026-2796 write-up); TechCrunch, The Register, Ars Technica, SecurityWeek, CNBC (April 7–8)
developments.capability: Anthropic's unreleased frontier model Claude Mythos Preview autonomously found thousands of high-severity zero-days across every major OS (Linux kernel, OpenBSD, FreeBSD) and every major web browser, converting 72.4% of found vulnerabilities into working exploits (vs ~0% for Claude Opus 4.6). Specific confirmed CVEs: CVE-2026-2796 (4-vuln Firefox chain, JIT heap spray, escaped renderer + OS sandboxes — full exploit published); CVE-2026-4747 (FreeBSD RCE, unauthenticated root, 17-year-old bug). Found a 27-year-old OpenBSD flaw that evaded 5 million prior automated tests. As of announcement, fewer than 1% of found vulnerabilities are patched — remainder under coordinated disclosure embargo. Project Glasswing: $100M in model-usage credits to 40+ coalition partners (AWS, Apple, Broadcom, Cisco, CrowdStrike, Google, JPMorgan, Linux Foundation, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Palo Alto Networks) for controlled defensive access only. Model not publicly available.
developments.caveats: Core exploit-conversion rate and vulnerability count are Anthropic self-reported. CVE-2026-2796 and CVE-2026-4747 provide independently checkable anchors (CVE numbers assigned, one exploit published). CrowdStrike and Linux Foundation publicly co-signed the initiative. The >99% unpatched bulk cannot be independently verified yet — under embargo. Treat specific CVEs as confirmed; the 'thousands of zero-days' aggregate count as likely until more disclosures land.
developments.scanner_note: MISSED IN INITIAL SCAN — research agent summarized the blog post title only and never fetched anthropic.com/glasswing or the system card. Adversarial filter was then misapplied: flagged 'Claude Mythos' as single-source instead of triggering deeper primary-source verification. Corrected on user report.

developments.title: Gemma 4 release + Google AI Edge Gallery (on-device iPhone inference)
developments.source: deepmind.google/models/gemma/gemma-4/; simonwillison.net (Google AI Edge Gallery, April 6)
developments.capability: Four model variants (2B, 4B, 26B MoE, 31B dense) under Apache 2.0. Built on Gemini 3 internals. 31B model ranks #3 on Arena AI text leaderboard (1452 Elo), beating models 20x its size. 256K context, multimodal (image + audio). Google AI Edge Gallery: official iPhone app for running Gemma 4 fully on-device with fast local inference.
developments.caveats: Arena AI Elo reflects community preference voting, not task-specific benchmarks. On-device performance is hardware-dependent (iPhone 15 Pro+ tier).

developments.title: Multi-agent social dynamics: conformity and persuasion measurably degrade collective LLM accuracy
developments.capability: Preprint shows conformity bias, perceived-expertise effects, and persuasion in LLM multi-agent collectives measurably degrade collective decision-making accuracy vs. individual agents.
developments.caveats: Preprint, not peer-reviewed. Effect sizes not confirmed. Track through peer review before updating neocortex orchestration architecture.

developments.title: GLM-5.1 (754B): emergent animated SVG generation without explicit prompting
developments.capability: Chinese AI lab released GLM-5.1 at 754B parameters. Spontaneously generates animated SVG with working CSS transforms without being prompted to animate.
developments.caveats: Single secondary source (Willison). Primary lab documentation not independently fetched. Few-prompt observation, not a systematic evaluation.

library_implications: Claude Mythos is the dominant signal this scan — a model that converts vulnerabilities into working exploits at 72% changes the threat model for any skill or infrastructure that touches external systems. This is directly relevant to neocortex (what agents can now do autonomously) and infrastructure (skills that make external calls or handle credentials face a different risk environment). The on-device Gemma 4 + multi-agent vulnerability paper are secondary signals. Scanner process note: initial scan failed to follow primary source links past blog post titles — a fetch-depth failure. Future scans must follow Anthropic announcement links to their full destination pages, not just skim blog titles.

headline: [ACTION NEEDED] Claude tool ecosystem goes GA + Sonnet 4.6 drops; AlphaEvolve demonstrates agent-driven algorithm discovery

developments.title: Claude Sonnet 4.6 + full tool ecosystem GA
developments.capability: 1M context window now GA (not beta) for Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6. Web search and web fetch tools now auto-write and execute code to filter results before they hit context window — a new paradigm where tools self-optimize their own output. Code execution, memory, programmatic tool calling, tool search, and tool use examples all moved from beta to GA. MCP connectors landed in Claude Excel (S&P Global, FactSet). Users preferred Sonnet 4.6 over 4.5 ~70% of the time in Claude Code.
developments.caveats: 1M context quality claim is weaker than GA status implies: Sonnet 4.5 dropped to 18.5% accuracy at 1M tokens (MRCR), and Anthropic has not published equivalent scores for 4.6. Independent testing shows Sonnet degrades noticeably past 400K. Use 1M for retrieval/indexing tasks; treat reasoning-at-1M as speculative until benchmarks land.

developments.title: AlphaEvolve: Gemini-powered evolutionary coding agent discovers and improves algorithms
developments.capability: DeepMind deployed an agent that combines Gemini Flash + Pro with automated evaluators and an evolutionary loop to discover and optimize algorithms. Verified real-world impact: recovered 0.7% of Google worldwide compute via better data center scheduling, 23% speedup on matrix multiplication (reducing Gemini training time 1%), 32.5% speedup on FlashAttention. On open math problems: rediscovered SOTA in 75% of cases, improved upon best-known solutions in 20%. Tackled the 300-year-old kissing number problem.
developments.caveats: Results are verified but self-reported by DeepMind on internal benchmarks. The 20% improvement rate on open problems is impressive but tested on a curated set — generalization to arbitrary domains is unverified. The system requires strong automated evaluators, which limits applicability to problems without clear scoring functions.

developments.title: GPT-5.4 mini and nano: efficient frontier models with built-in computer use
developments.capability: GPT-5.4 mini brings near-frontier coding performance (54% SWE-bench Pro vs 57.7% full model) at ~6x cost reduction. Built-in computer use and tool search. GPT-5.4 nano for high-volume, simple tasks. OpenAI APIs now process 15B tokens/minute. Codex at 2M weekly users, 5x growth in 3 months.
developments.caveats: No independently published HumanEval scores — OpenAI hasn't released public HumanEval benchmarks for GPT-5 family. Performance comparison charts use compressed Y-axes. SWE-bench Pro numbers appear to be OpenAI self-reported. Context quality collapses past 64K-256K on mini. Treat mini as confirmed; specific benchmark numbers as directional.

developments.title: Open-source AI: Qwen dominates HuggingFace derivatives; sovereign AI accelerating
developments.capability: Qwen is now the most-forked base model on HuggingFace with 113k+ derivative models (vs Llama 27k, DeepSeek 6k). South Korean national champions (LG AI Research, SK Telecom, Naver Cloud) now trending alongside Chinese models. Western developers racing to provide commercially deployable alternatives (OpenAI GPT-OSS, AI2 OLMo, Google Gemma). Model/dataset repository count approaching 2x growth from one year ago.
developments.caveats: HuggingFace derivative counts measure popularity/forkability, not capability quality. Qwen dominance in derivatives does not necessarily mean Qwen is the best base model. Sovereign AI initiatives are in early stages.

library_implications: Two skills need immediate attention. (1) Any skill relying on tool use or search should be updated to reflect the new GA status — web search now filters via auto-generated code execution, which changes token efficiency assumptions. Neocortex skills (frontier-scanner, spelunker) should note this capability. (2) AlphaEvolve is a proof point for autonomous research agents that could inform a new 'algorithm-discovery' or 'agentic-research' skill archetype — particularly relevant for the research and data-science domains. The 1M context window going GA expands what long-context skills can promise, but skills should note the quality degradation caveat past 400K until Anthropic publishes MRCR scores for 4.6.
